name: A2-02 Replay-safe recovery - re-run without doing the work twice

meta.description: After a failure you re-run the workflow. Everything it already did successfully happens again unless something stops it. This is the guard: a durable record of which business events have been processed, checked before the side effect rather than after it.
meta.builtFor: n8n Code node typeVersion 2, HTTP Request node typeVersion 4.2
meta.author: Suyash Raj - https://rajsuyash.com/blog/n8n-error-handling-best-practices.html
meta.setup: None. Run it, then run it again.
meta.expectedOutput: First run: 3 items marked new, 3 POSTs sent. Second run with the same input: 0 new, 0 POSTs, 3 skipped. The 'Recovery report' node prints both counts.
meta.failureCases: Comment out the seen-key write in 'Skip what was already done' and run twice - the second run sends all 3 again, which is the bug this workflow exists to prevent. Change one orderId and only that one is treated as new.
meta.limits: getWorkflowStaticData is stored with the workflow on this n8n instance. It is fine for dedupe windows measured in hours or days and for a single instance. For multi-instance deployments, long retention, or anything financial, keep the processed-key record in the destination system or a database the destination shares, so the guard survives an instance rebuild.

nodes.name: Skip what was already done
nodes.notes: Claiming before the side effect trades one failure mode for a strictly cheaper one: a crash between the claim and the POST means one order is skipped and must be replayed deliberately. The alternative - claiming after - means one order is charged twice. Under-delivering is recoverable; double-charging is not.

nodes.name: Do the side effect
nodes.notes: Two independent guards, deliberately. The static-data record stops US repeating the call; the Idempotency-Key lets the SERVER reject it if we do anyway. Either one alone has a gap the other covers.
